title: Thermodynamic phase transition, pairing symmetry and Fermi surface topology in Ruddlesden-Popper nickelate films
authors: Yu Miao, Zhiwei Wang, Hongxu Sun, Jianchang Shen, Runqing Luan, Zhipeng Ou, Xinru Yong, Zhenyu Wang, Tao Wu, Haoyu Hu, Junfeng He, Xianhui Chen
abstract: Ruddlesden-Popper (RP) nickelates provide an uncharted territory to explore high-transition-temperature (high-$T_C$) superconductivity and superconducting mechanism. Here, we investigate the electronic structure of a new type of high-$T_C$ superconducting RP nickelate heterostructure $\mathrm{La_2PrNi_2O_7/NdAlO_3}$ by angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. A superconducting state is observed without a pseudogap state, enabling a direct measurement of the superconducting order parameter and a microscopic extraction of the electronic specific heat. The observed superconducting gap opens at $T_C$ with prominent coherence peaks, illustrating the emergence of nonzero order parameter upon entering the superconducting state. An electronic specific heat jump appears at $T_C$, further demonstrating a thermodynamic phase transition. The magnitude of the superconducting order parameter is quantified by the observed superconducting coherence peaks, and a nodeless behavior is unambiguously established in the absence of pseudogap. The underlying Fermi surface consists of $α$, $β$ and $γ$ pockets, exhibiting a multi-orbital nature. Strain dependent measurements further reveal the $γ$ pocket in all superconducting and non-superconducting films with different epitaxial strain. Our results establish the missing thermodynamic evidence for superconducting phase transition in nickelates. They also provide direct evidence for the symmetry of the superconducting order parameter and illustrate the relationship between Fermi surface topology and the emergence of superconductivity in RP nickelate films.
summary: This work investigates superconductivity in RP nickelate films using ARPES and thermodynamic analysis. The authors report direct evidence for a superconducting phase transition via an electronic specific heat jump, confirming a nonzero order parameter. They establish that the pairing symmetry is nodeless (s-wave) and map how the Fermi surface topology relates to this emergent superconducting state.
main_problem: To investigate high-transition-temperature superconductivity and determine the pairing symmetry in Ruddlesden-Popper nickelate films, specifically by providing direct thermodynamic evidence of the superconducting phase transition.
main_result: The study observed a clear electronic specific heat jump at T_C, confirming a thermodynamic phase transition, and established that the superconducting gap is nodeless, suggesting an s-wave pairing symmetry in these RP nickelates.
method: The research combines Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements with Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations to probe electronic structure and thermodynamics.
model_or_system: The physical system is the Ruddlesden-Popper (RP) nickelate heterostructure, $	ext{La}_2	ext{PrNi}_2	ext{O}_7/	ext{NdAlO}_3$, thin films. Measurements are performed on these epitaxial films under varying strain conditions.
key_observables: Superconducting gap magnitude ($\Delta \sim 16 	ext{ meV}$), electronic specific heat jump at $T_C$, and the topology of the Fermi surface pockets ($\alpha,  eta, \gamma$).
important_parameters: Critical temperature ($T_C$), superconducting order parameter, epitaxial strain, and orbital character (e.g., $	ext{dz}^2$ pocket).
main_assumptions: The electronic specific heat analysis relies on analogies with cuprates; DFT calculations often assume a single-layer limit to simplify the model.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate ARPES results showing gap opening, temperature dependence of the gap, evidence for the specific heat jump at $T_C$, and how Fermi surface pockets evolve under varying epitaxial strain.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by characterizing the electronic structure via ARPES, demonstrating the superconducting transition through thermodynamic measurements (specific heat), determining the pairing symmetry from the gap structure, and finally mapping the relationship between Fermi surface topology and superconductivity using strain dependence.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state physics, the clear measurement of a phase transition signature ($\Delta C/T$) and the determination of pairing symmetry provide fundamental insights into emergent quantum ground states relevant to strongly correlated electron systems.
